nodes: ABPI: is there disease, how bad?

visuals.title: Watershed sites break down first
visuals.text: Narrowed arteries leave the most distal tissue (toes, heel, lateral malleolus) with the least perfusion.

visuals.title: Why it looks punched out
nodes: Little blood flow: dry, pale base

visuals.title: Why antiplatelet and statin
visuals.text: Clopidogrel stops platelets; atorvastatin slows plaque growth, breaking the loop.

glossary.hyperlipidaemia: Raised levels of fats such as cholesterol in the blood.
glossary.toes: The most distal part of the foot, first to lose blood supply in PAD.
glossary.calf claudication: Cramping calf pain on walking that eases with rest, from inadequate arterial supply.
glossary.reduced pulses: Weak or absent foot pulses, suggesting narrowed arteries upstream.
glossary.peripheral pulses: Pulses felt in the limbs, such as femoral, popliteal, dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial.
glossary.hair loss: Loss of leg hair from chronic poor blood supply to the follicles.
glossary.shiny skin: Thin, smooth, tight skin from chronic ischaemia.
glossary.atrophic: Wasted or thinned from loss of cells.
glossary.exudative: Leaking fluid; typical of venous ulcers.
glossary.aspirin: Antiplatelet drug that irreversibly blocks COX, reducing platelet clumping.
glossary.lipid-lowering therapy: Drugs, usually statins, that lower cholesterol.
glossary.supervised exercise programme: Structured walking exercise that improves claudication by building collateral circulation.
glossary.smoking cessation: Stopping smoking, the single most important risk factor change in PAD.
glossary.opioid: Strong painkiller acting on opioid receptors, such as morphine.
glossary.morphine: Strong opioid painkiller used for severe pain.
glossary.paracetamol: Simple painkiller, first step on the analgesic ladder.
glossary.distal: Further from the centre of the body.
glossary.tissue death: Death of cells in an area of tissue, also called necrosis.
glossary.arterial insufficiency: Arterial blood supply too low to meet the tissue's needs.
glossary.cardiovascular events: Heart attacks, strokes and similar arterial events.
glossary.atherosclerotic: Caused by fatty plaques in artery walls.
glossary.intervention: A procedure, such as angioplasty or bypass, to treat the blockage.
glossary.thrombus: Blood clot formed inside a vessel.
glossary.platelets: Small blood cells that clump together to start a clot.
glossary.plaque: Fatty, fibrous deposit in an artery wall.
glossary.arterioles: Small arteries that control blood flow into capillaries.
glossary.elevation: Raising the leg above heart level.
glossary.aorta: Main artery leaving the heart, often affected by atherosclerosis upstream of leg arteries.
glossary.ulcer: A break in the skin or mucosa that fails to heal.
